keyVerseText: The children of Zaccai, seven hundred and threescore.
rootMeaning: The root of זַכַּי (Zakkay) comes from the Hebrew root זָכַךְ (zâkak), which conveys the idea of being pure, clean, or bright. This root emphasizes not only physical cleanliness but also moral and spiritual purity or transparency. Thus, the name Zakkay literally carries the sense of one who is purified or made clean, highlighting a deeper dimension of integrity and holiness beyond the simple English gloss of 'pure.'
usageInScripture: The word זַכַּי appears twice in Scripture, consistently translated as 'of Zaccai,' referring specifically to a proper name. It identifies an Israelite family head among the returning exiles, emphasizing lineage and community restoration. This consistent usage underscores the importance of this figure and his family in the post-exilic period, linking the name's meaning of purity with the faithful remnant returning to Jerusalem.
theologicalSignificance: The name Zakkay, rooted in purity, reflects the biblical theme of God's people being called to holiness and cleansing. In the context of the returned exiles, it symbolizes the spiritual renewal and restoration God brings to His covenant community. For the Christian faith, this purity points forward to the ultimate cleansing through Christ, who purifies believers and makes them a holy people. Recognizing this name's meaning enriches our understanding of God's redemptive work in history and His call for His people to live pure lives in obedience to Him.
keyVerseReflection: Ezra 2:9 notes, 'The children of Zaccai, seven hundred and threescore,' highlighting the sizeable family led by Zakkay among the returning exiles. The use of this name here accentuates not just a genealogical record but the presence of a purified remnant, set apart and restored. It reminds readers that those who return to God are called to embody purity and faithfulness as part of the renewed covenant community.
